sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cloud Vulnerability Scanning and Penetration Testing SaaS

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Franco-Belgian Napoleonic tradition, unitary national jurisdiction with EU-law primacy and no sub-state fiscal distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States Income Tax Treaty of 3 April 1996 (as amended by the 2004 and 2009 Protocols)
Belgium–Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) Bilateral Investment Treaties with over 60 contracting states
Luxembourg–China Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion (1994, as amended by the 2019 Protocol)
Luxembourg–France, Luxembourg–Germany, Luxembourg–Netherlands and Luxembourg–Switzerland Double Taxation Agreements
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures (MLI), ratified by Luxembourg as a Covered Tax Agreement framework

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended by the Laws of 27 October 2010, 13 February 2013, 30 June 2015, 23 August 2017, 25 March 2020, 26 January 2021 and 16 June 2022) implementing EU Directives 2015/849, (EU) 2018/843 and (EU) 2018/1673; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 August 2019 on the RBE functioning; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (as amended by the Law of 23 September 2020 reforming the SARL); CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended); EU restrictive-measures Regulations implementing UN Security Council and EU sanctions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the Articles of Association (Statuts) of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official corporate registry of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the Convention of 5 October 1961 where the country of origin is a Contracting State; otherwise Consular Legalization by the Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / certificate of existence of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent commercial authority in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, with an original wet signature and stamp.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the board or shareholders' resolution authorizing the incorporation of the Luxembourg SARL, the funding of the capital and the appointment of the Luxembourg manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary and notary public of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of valid passports or national identity cards of the proposed managers, shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport or identity authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy certified by a notary public, then Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record extract (casier judiciaire / certificate of good conduct) of each proposed manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National criminal records registry of the manager's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; for Luxembourg residents the extract is obtained directly from the Luxembourg criminal records service.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and confirmation of source of funds for the capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank holding the shareholder's funding account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer's signature notarized and authenticated by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of address of each ultimate beneficial owner (utility bill, bank statement or lease agreement, dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, bank or notary of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory at pre-incorporation onboarding: (i) PEP screening of all shareholders, managers and UBOs against the CSSF/FIU PEP databases, international PEP lists and open-source negative media under Article 5 and related provisions of the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02, with enhanced due diligence required for PEPs, their family members and known close associates; (ii) sanctions screening against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council consolidated lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists (required for any USD wire-transfer rail) and the Luxembourg FIU national alert list; (iii) source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification via audited financial statements, bank references and capital-funding trail; (iv) negative-news and adverse-media checks; (v) ongoing monitoring obligations for the notary, the bank and the domiciliation agent under AMLD5/AMLD6 and CSSF Regulation 12-02.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), electronic filing portal at https://www.lbr.lu; the RCS, RBE and RESA modules are operated within the LBR online system.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must be expressed in Latin characters and may be drafted in Luxembourgish, French, German, English or another language; if a non-Latin script is used, a statutory transliteration in Latin characters must be submitted and must not be confusingly similar to prior registered names. The name must include the legal-form suffix 'société à responsabilité limitée' or its accepted abbreviation 'S.à r.l.' / 'SARL', must not mislead the public, must respect public order (ordre public), and must pass the distinction test against all prior names in the LBR Central Index.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Luxembourg' or any combination suggesting affiliation with the Grand Duchy (prior ministerial authorization of the Ministry of Justice / Ministry of the Economy required)
'banque', 'bank', 'assurance', 'réassurance', 'securitisation', 'fonds d'investissement', 'fonds de placement', 'OPC' (prior CSSF or Ministry of Finance authorization required)
'fiduciaire', 'trust', 'gestion de fortune', 'conseiller en investissements', 'asset management' (regulated PFS/AML markers not approvable for an unlicensed cybersecurity SaaS)
'état', 'Etat', 'chambre', 'administration publique', 'université', 'EU', 'NATO', 'ONU', 'OCDE' (protected sovereign, public and institutional markers)
'euro', 'monnaie', 'banque centrale', 'central bank' (monetary-authority markers prohibited without explicit statutory approval)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RCS name reservation, filed through the LBR portal, is valid for 2 months and may be renewed on payment of the standard tariff for additional successive 2-month periods, providing a practical maximum pre-registration window of at least 4 months. If the proposed name is rejected for identity, confusing similarity or non-compliance with public-order naming rules, the applicant shall: (i) file a written reconsideration request with the LBR Registry Office (Service du RCS) within 15 days of the refusal, presenting revised name submissions; (ii) obtain the competent ministerial or regulatory pre-approval where the name contains a sensitive token; (iii) submit a formal administrative appeal (recours en annulation) before the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within 3 months of notification of the final refusal, pursuant to Articles 4 to 6 of the Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS; alternatively, (iv) where the conflict arises against a prior registered right-holder, the applicant may obtain a written no-objection consent of that right-holder for expedited re-admission of the name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office without a physical Luxembourg situs is not acceptable as the statutory registered office under Articles 161 and 186 of the consolidated Law of 10 August 1915. The SARL must maintain a real, physical address in Luxembourg at which the statutory books, share register, accounting records and corporate documents are accessible and at which legal process and administrative service can be effected. Professional domiciliation under the Law of 31 May 1999 by a Ministry-of-Justice-approved domiciliation agent is expressly permissible and is the accepted market practice for a remote-first cybersecurity SaaS, provided the agent operates a physical Luxembourg office, provides registered-agent and mail-handling services, retains the statutory records and supports UBO-compliance duties; the domiciliation agreement and the identity of the authorized registered agent must be notified to the RCS.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical or documentary verification probability is assessed at approximately 12% per operating year for a low-risk, license-free IT-services company; cumulative probability of at least one RCS, RBE, Administration de l'enregistrement, des douanes et des accises (AED) or CSSF-related spot-check over a 3-year horizon is estimated at approximately 31%. The domiciliation agent must retain on site the UBO diligence file, the share register, board resolutions and evidence of commercial substance for inspection readiness.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name availability search and name reservation (réserve de nom) at the LBR/RCS portal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Grand-Ducal Regulation on LBR/RCS fees implementing the Law of 19 December 2002 (approximately EUR 20 plus VAT)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial incorporation deed (acte constitutif) for a standard multi-shareholder SARL, including drafting, reading, signature formalities, legalization of founder signatures and notarial minutes
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff scale plus disbursements; EUR 2,000–2,800 prevailing market benchmark for a standard SARL incorporating with corporate shareholders

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration filing fee for submission of the notarial deed, legal form, managers' appointments and registered-office declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: LBR statutory registration tariff for a commercial company (EUR 75–80)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation deed in the electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), operated by LBR

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration filing in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) for individuals and legal-entity shareholders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: RBE filing is free of charge; online submission due within one month from RCS registration pursuant to the Law of 13 January 2019

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translations into French or English of foreign corporate documents, passports, criminal records and bank reference letters
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator registered on the Luxembourg courts' official list
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 60–120 per certified page; 2–4 pages typical for a standard shareholder pack

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization bundle for 6–8 foreign-origin documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority in the country of origin (e.g., U.S. Secretary of State, UK FCDO) or Luxembourg consular post for non-Hague-Convention states
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-document apostille tariffs (USD 2–20 per document) plus courier, consular file and handling charges; USD 50–80 per document bundle benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foreign criminal record certificates (casiers judiciaires) of each proposed manager
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: National criminal record registries of the managers' countries of residence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Foreign government statutory fee of USD 20–60 per extract plus certified translation; typical for two proposed managers

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / domiciliation service for the first full year through an authorized domiciliation agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EUR 180–250 per month, including physical Luxembourg address, mail handling, statutory books custody, registered-agent service and UBO-compliance support

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds verification package required by the notary and the opening bank
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Emitting bank of the shareholder's funding account
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff for a reference or attestation letter (EUR 30–120 per letter) plus notarized signature authentication

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External corporate counsel fee for Stage-1 due diligence, UBO piercing analysis, AML/KYC legal review, name-clearance coordination and notary instruction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg corporate law firm registered with the Luxembourg Bar (Barreau de Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EUR 250–350 per hour; fixed-fee standard SARL Stage-1 package of EUR 3,000–4,000

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as consolidated and amended; SARL regime under Articles 100 et seq. (Société à Responsabilité Limitée).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS Luxembourg), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) through the eJustice/LBR online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Authentic notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif authentique) submitted for RCS registration via the LBR electronic filing system; registration extract published in RESA.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed and paid-up capital of EUR 12,000 for an SARL, fully paid at subscription; funds must be deposited in a blocked bank account or escrow and released only after RCS registration; in-kind contributions require a statutory auditor's report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the first meeting of the shareholders and managers of [COMPANY] S.à r.l., held at the registered office on [date], the following resolutions were adopted unanimously: (1) the share subscription set out in the notarial articles of association is approved and confirmed, the shares being fully paid-up; (2) the registered office at [address], Luxembourg, and the corporate purpose, including information technology consultancy, cloud services, and cybersecurity software-as-a-service, are adopted; (3) [NAME] is appointed as manager (gérant) with sole signature authority to represent the company; and (4) all RCS registration, RESA publication, and ancillary filing steps are authorized. All preparatory acts and documents are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation file preparation and corporate name clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg) and LBR corporate-name availability check
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Luxembourg notary to draft the French-language articles of association. Reserve and police-check the corporate name with LBR. Confirm the SARL name, registered office address, corporate purpose aligned with ISIC 6201, share allocation, and proposed managers. Notary verifies identity and capacity of signatories.
required_dossiers: Registered office address and lessor consent letter
Passport or ID copies of all shareholders and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or RCS notes an irregularity, the notary resubmits with a corrected draft or an alternative name; no filing fee is lost at this pre-submission stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit in blocked escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CSSF-regulated Luxembourg credit institution or notary's escrow/client account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Each shareholder transfers the cash contribution to a blocked account opened for the future SARL. Account documentation must state that funds are reserved until the RCS registration certificate is issued. The bank or notary issues a written confirmation of paid-up capital and the irrevocable blocking arrangement.
required_dossiers: Corporate/entity ID documents if shareholder is a legal person
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a transfer is delayed or the certificate is incomplete, the bank issues a corrected blocked-funds confirmation and the notary reschedules the deed execution date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of authentic notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All subscribers or their duly authorised attorneys appear before the notary. The notary reads and verifies the articles, confirms capital payment, and executes the deed. Certified copies are produced. If contributions are in-kind, the notary requires the statutory auditor's report filed with the notary before execution.
required_dossiers: Powers of attorney if acting by proxy
Statutory auditor's report for in-kind contributions, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed contains procedural defects, the notary draws a corrective rider before RCS submission or, if necessary, executes a fresh deed with shareholder consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing and registration with RCS Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) RCS electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Notary submits the authenticated deed and mandatory RCS forms through the LBR system, pays applicable state fees, and requests registration. RCS verifies legal conformity, assigns the RCS registration number and business identification number, and issues the registration extract which confers legal personality.
required_dossiers: UBO filings for the register of beneficial owners
RCS filing form signed by a manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RCS issues a query or formal notice, the notary and manager file the requested clarifications or amending extracts through the LBR portal before the statutory cure deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official electronic compendium of companies and associations (RESA), published via LBR/Mémorial
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: RCS transmits the registration extract to RESA. The company verifies that the publication is complete and correct. The RESA publication together with the RCS extract is used as evidence of incorporation for banks, clients, and public administrations.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication contains a typographical or legal variance, the company files a request for correction with LBR, and the notary files any necessary rectification act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, social security, and data-protection onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA; Administration des contributions directes; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Commission nationale pour la protection des données (CNPD) as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for VAT and corporate income tax, obtain the Luxembourg VAT number, enroll managers/employees with CCSS, and confirm the UBO register is updated. For cybersecurity SaaS, verify GDPR compliance and any personal-data processing documentation but no special operating permit is required; if employees are hired, submit workplace declarations to ITM.
required_dossiers: VAT registration form and tax questionnaire
Employer registration data for CCSS, if applicable
GDPR processing records and DPO designation, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or CCSS numbers are delayed, follow up in writing and submit duplicate filings; any assessment error can be corrected via a request for administrative reconsideration before the relevant administration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Direction de l'industrie et de la compétitivité) — consulted only if future activities enter manufacturing; not applicable for cloud SaaS.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating licence is required for ISIC 6201 cybersecurity software-as-a-service; RCS registration and GDPR compliance constitute the applicable go-to-market conditions.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based cloud SaaS has no installation falling within EIA categories under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 May 2017.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to this activity; if an office lease generates ordinary waste, apply the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste management and municipal collection rules; no wastewater, VOC, or industrial emission thresholds are triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No civil defense clearance is required for a virtual/cloud service; verify the lessor's building fire-safety certification, register employees, and if physical office premises are used, comply with ITM workplace safety standards under the Luxembourg Labor Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT. Digital services: MyGuichet.lu, eTVA filing portal, RCS/BRC business register
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The SARL is registered with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through a notary and appointed approved statutory auditor where required. Upon RCS registration the ACD issues a Luxembourg corporate tax identification number (N° d'identification national). For VAT, the SARL must file Form 510a with the AEDT to obtain a Luxembourg VAT number before invoicing, intra-EU acquisitions, imports, or e-service supplies. Non-resident foreign entities supplying taxable services into Luxembourg with a fixed establishment or economic nexus must similarly register via a Luxembourg authorised representative and provide proof of non-resident status and place-of-supply documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. The SARL is per se opaque and taxable at entity level. Available elections: Luxembourg tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) for a 95%+ owned Luxembourg subsidiary group, VAT grouping election as a single taxable person under Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT law, and parent-subsidiary participation exemption election. ATAD hybrid mismatch rules may preclude or neutralise elective payment/classification outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover for the domestic small-business exemption; no threshold for foreign businesses with a Luxembourg fixed establishment or deemed establishment. Non-Union OSS optional for EU B2C e-services; Union OSS for intra-EU B2C supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national real-time fiscal clearance/API/stamping mandate exists. Electronic invoicing is accepted and encouraged. Mandatory PEPPOL-compliant e-invoicing (UBL or Factur-X via PEPPOL network) applies for B2G invoices and public procurement contracts. Standard EU VAT e-invoicing rules apply; invoices must include VAT details and reverse-charge or zero-rating references.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported outside the European Union qualify for 0% VAT with proof of dispatch/transport. Electronically supplied services, cybersecurity SaaS, cloud vulnerability scanning, and penetration testing qualify as 'electronically supplied services' under Article 58 of the EU VAT Directive. B2B supplies to a non-Luxembourg EU VAT-registered customer fall under the reverse-charge procedure; B2B or B2C supplies addressed to a customer outside the EU/territorial scope may be zero-rated if the supplier proves the customer's establishment and effective receipt of the service at that overseas location. Pure domestic supplies are taxable at 17% standard rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs/Intrastat Export Declaration (SAD/DE-507) where goods are simultaneously exported
Transport documents: Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, or CMR consignment note
Commercial invoice with explicit zero-rating / reverse-charge annotation
Executed service contract or order form evidencing the customer's non-Luxembourg/non-EU establishment
Proof of customer's foreign VAT ID or TIN where available
Payment and inward remittance evidence: bank transfer, SWIFT/SEPA records, card settlement statements
Technical records: IP logs, server location metadata, access logs substantiating the place of effective use and enjoyment outside Luxembourg
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg tax authorities may retrospectively disallow zero-rating and reassess standard-rate VAT plus default interest and penalties for a five-year limitation period (ten years for tax fraud). Penalties range from administrative fines under the Luxembourg tax code (Abo) and VAT law up to EUR 250,000, and criminal penalties including imprisonment for wilful evasion or fraudulent false export declarations. Clawback may include the full under-collected VAT, interest, and disqualification from future zero-rating treatment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB); prudential and AML conduct oversight is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility without exchange controls. The Euro (EUR) is freely floated and fungible; Luxembourg maintains no capital or current account convertibility restrictions, benefiting from complete capital-movement liberalization under TFEU Article 63. Profit remittance is frictionless: dividends, interest, and fees may be transferred abroad without prior central-bank approval, subject only to the corporate-law net-asset distribution test (Luxembourg Companies Act Art. 725-1) and the receiving bank's AML clearance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. There is no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation for export proceeds or foreign-currency receipts (USD, GBP). The SARL may freely retain, convert, or hold proceeds in any EU-authorized credit institution or passported payment institution.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) and Operational EUR/USD Account
Operational Account with SME e-banking and direct API
Operational Account and trade finance facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High as an ancillary collection rail, but Low as a primary settlement bank. EU/EEA-licensed electronic money institutions (e.g., Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer) holding a valid PSD2 passport lodged with the CSSF may lawfully open EUR payment accounts and process SaaS payouts; however, an offshore digital EMI without a European passport cannot legally hold segregated EUR accounts nor settle funds for the SARL. The core treasury account structure must remain at a CSSF-licensed credit institution to preserve creditworthiness, evidence treasury centralization for Luxembourg tax purposes, and avoid concentration risk on unregulated custodians.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors who are non-EU residents must generally attend an in-person KYC interview at the Luxembourg branch or at the bank's foreign correspondent office; remote video identity verification is increasingly accepted by BIL and ING, but only when combined with notarized signatures, apostilled corporate extracts, and LEI validation. A locally appointed manager (managing director) with signatory authority can meaningfully reduce the physical-presence burden. Budget 2–3 weeks for full onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) with cross-border digital revenue, thin local substance, and limited established banking history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of UBO register extract, LEI certificate, three years of audited financials of the shareholder, notarized capital subscription agreement, source-of-wealth documentation (asset sale agreements, gift deeds, loan contracts), board minutes appointing a Luxembourg resident AML officer, tax residence certificates, CRS/FATCA self-certifications, and a Luxembourg Barreau legal opinion confirming commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume SaaS revenue settled through Stripe payment facilitator rails, potentially obscuring the underlying card-acquiring chain across non-EU countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Annotated business plan and B2B client list with country risk ratings, standard customer SaaS agreement demonstrating pure license/subscription income (no e-money float or custodial activity), SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certificates, a treasury flow diagram tracing payouts from Stripe to the operational account, and an external auditor's confirmation that payment facilitation is ancillary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Share capital injection routed from a related holding entity without an evident commercial due-diligence trail, inclusive of share-premium classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Escrow release instruction countersigned by the notary, published accounts of the shareholder, intercompany loan agreement (if debt element exists), capital subscription receipts signed by the general manager, RCS registration certificate, tax advice confirming the share premium treatment, and evidence that the EUR 12,000 minimum capital requirement under Art. 710-1 of the Luxembourg Companies Act is met.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant SWIFT MT103 wire denominated in EUR to the blocked capital-escrow account at BGL BNP Paribas, with clear purpose codes 'SCAP' or 'Capital subscription' and a reference to the notarial deed; no commercial invoice should be attached. The remitting shareholder and its ordering bank must satisfy the beneficiary bank's KYC and sanctions screening (OFAC, EU, UN); transfers exceeding EUR 10,000 trigger enhanced reporting. The contribution is evidenced by the notary's certificate (déclaration de souscription et de libération) filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), after which the funds are released to the operational account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic and SEPA suppliers to be settled via SEPAmax/MT103 through the TARGET2 real-time gross settlement system; non-EUR vendor payments (notably USD) to use the bank's USD correspondent account with SWIFT MT103 confirmation and same-day value dating. For hardware or co-licensing procurement exceeding EUR 50,000 from non-EEA vendors, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit under UCP600 is recommended. Liquidity policy requires a daily automated sweep from the USD Stripe collection account into the EUR operational account, executed at the ECB reference rate only after a defined exposure threshold is reached.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) executed under a standard master forward contract without ISDA, subject to the bank's credit line and FX-only settlement risk lien.
European-style FX Options (plain vanilla, cash-settled) to protect multi-year USD-denominated licensing agreements and fixed-budget procurement.

Cross-currency Swaps (EUR/USD) permitted under ISDA 2002 master agreement with a credit support annex, relying on the EMIR Article 10 clearing exemption for non-financial counterparties below the clearing threshold.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) permissible solely for exotic third-country currency exposures (e.g., KRW, INR) arising from non-EU supplier contracts; prohibited by bank policy for EUR/USD given full euro deliverability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (annual accounts) with list of SARL shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés / Central Balance Sheet Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval and no later than seven months after financial year-end (calendar year: approval by 30 June and filing by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines of EUR 250 to EUR 5,000; court-ordered deposit; risk of administrative strike-off after two consecutive missing annual filings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of Ultimate Beneficial Owner details in the RBE register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every 12 months from the last UBO registration or confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EUR 5,000 and/or imprisonment for deliberate non-compliance; administrative penalties issued by the RBE authority

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for SARLs exceeding at least two of three size criteria for two consecutive years: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average 50 employees; also required for public-interest entities. Smaller SARLs may be exempt if no statutory audit threshold is met.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial accounts, as amended, transposing EU Accounting Directives); IFRS permitted for consolidated accounts and listed entities only.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each UBO must confirm RBE data every 12 months after initial filing or previous confirmation; changes in shareholding or control must be filed within one month of knowledge. The annual confirmation serves as attestation of continued accuracy.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE internal register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 – 2,500 (typical annual domiciliation and corporate agency service)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – 15,000 (only when statutory audit thresholds are exceeded)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Luxembourg corporate income tax (IRC) is levied at a flat 17% for taxable profits above EUR 175,000; the first EUR 175,000 is taxed at 15%. A 7% solidarity surcharge is added to the CIT liability, producing a national effective rate of 18.19%. The municipal business tax is imposed by each commune at rates between 6.75% and 11.3%, typically 6.75% in Luxembourg City. The combined nominal effective rate for a Luxembourg City SARL is approximately 24.94%. An Innovation Box regime exempts 80% of qualifying IP-derived income (patents, cybersecurity software, qualifying intangibles), yielding an effective rate of approximately 5.76% for eligible IP income. Additional incentives include super-deductions for R&D and an investment tax credit of up to 8% for qualifying investments. Tax losses may be carried forward indefinitely under Luxembourg domestic law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 500 – Annual corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (IS), and net wealth tax (IFF) declaration, filed electronically via the ACD e-filing platform 'eCDF' (Electronic Corporate Tax Declaration) through MyGuichet.lu or the professional tax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six (6) months after the end of the fiscal year. For calendar-year taxpayers, the statutory deadline is 30 June of the following year; the ACD routinely grants an administratively extendable deadline to 31 December on standard request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification – legal name, RCS registration number, Luxembourg tax number (matricule), registered office, and fiscal year end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident company filing only for a Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) must identify the PE and its local tax representative; companies without a PE must not file Form 500.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statements declaration – global net result (profit or loss) per statutory accounts prepared under Luxembourg GAAP (LUX GAAP).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Restrict the result to the Luxembourg PE's local profit and loss; include intercompany transactions and PE-specific allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments – add-back of non-deductible expenses (e.g., fines, donations, 50% of entertainment costs, excessive management fees, amounts subject to inadequate withholding).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same adjustments to the PE's taxable base; ensure all intercompany payments satisfy the arm's length standard and evidence burden.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and exemptions – participation exemption on dividends and capital gains, Innovation Box 80% IP deduction, R&D super-deduction, investment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies may claim these only for income attributable to the Luxembourg PE; IP and R&D reliefs require substance and tracking of qualifying revenues.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base computation – current-year taxable profit after adjustments, deductible loss carryforward utilized, and remaining losses available for future offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Show the PE's current net income and offset of prior PE losses; loss utilization limited to PE-source income and subject to continuity of ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction disclosure – description of intercompany financing, IP licensing, SaaS subscription revenue splitting, cost-sharing, and management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose transactions between the non-resident head office and the Luxembourg PE; attach a functional and risk analysis under OECD TP guidelines.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties range from EUR 100 to EUR 25,000, with an automatic EUR 10 daily penalty after the formal demand (capped at EUR 25,000). Late payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month. If the ACD makes an ex officio assessment, the understatement may be increased by up to 100% of the tax evaded. Willful failure to file is a criminal tax offence.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive rate, the beneficial owner must submit a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its jurisdiction of residence, a completed ownership/beneficial ownership attestation, and any limitation-of-benefits declaration under the applicable DTA. The submission must be made to the Luxembourg paying agent before payment to obtain relief at source. Alternatively, the excess withholding may be reclaimed through the ACD refund procedure under Article 242 LIR, with the TRC and proof of entitlement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties – domestic exemption: Luxembourg imposes no source withholding tax on royalty or licence payments to non-residents. Treaty rates typically range from 0% to 5%, and the EU Interest-Royalties Directive provides 0% withholding between associated EU companies. Interest – domestic exemption: no withholding tax on interest paid to non-residents, unless the debt is profit-participating, in which case it is treated as a dividend and subject to 15% WHT. Treaty interest rates generally range from 0% to 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File – mandatory for groups with consolidated annual revenue exceeding EUR 50,000,000. Local File – mandatory for Luxembourg entities where the aggregate annual value of controlled transactions exceeds EUR 500,000 (or EUR 1,000,000 for financial transactions), as set out in administrative guidance. Country-by-Country Report – required for multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies economic substance standards through the OECD/BEPS framework, the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) transposition, and the domestic General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR). The ACD may disregard artificial arrangements lacking real business purpose and economic substance (Articles 6 AStG and 106 LIR). For a cybersecurity SaaS SARL, evidence of substance includes local office premises, qualified technical staff exercising cybersecurity product development and client oversight, hosting infrastructure decisions, management of SaaS contracts and risk, and local bank accounts. IP-holding and financing entities are particularly scrutinized. A shell company without these substance indicators is exposed to treaty denial, reclassification of income, additional assessments, and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing false or incomplete Luxembourg corporate tax returns, concealing SaaS subscription revenue, forging invoices or expense records, or misrepresenting the EPS or Cybersecurity service revenue to lower taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 250,000 and/or imprisonment for one to five years (Articles 39 and 40 LIR). Civil re-assessment of evaded tax plus an administrative fine of 10% to 100% of the evaded tax; late interest at 0.6% per month; court conviction may be published; professional licence restrictions apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, managers, and de facto officers face criminal liability and can have the corporate veil pierced for fraudulent conduct. Personal assets may be seized to settle tax restitution; travel bans may be imposed; imprisonment is available for aggravated fraud; civil restitution orders against natural persons.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold and Remit Dividend WHT
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends to non-resident shareholders without collecting the 15% statutory withholding tax, or without verifying treaty or EU Directive relief eligibility, or intentionally routing payments to shell entities to avoid WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The unpaid WHT becomes a corporate debt; ACD may impose administrative penalties up to 10% of the withheld amount, late interest of 0.6% per month, and joint and several assessment against the company and its officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Luxembourg enforcement rules, the responsible manager or director is personally liable for withheld taxes not remitted to the treasury. The benefit of inventory does not apply, enabling direct seizure of directors' personal bank accounts and assets; misuse of corporate assets may also trigger criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany royalties, management fees, financing margins, or SaaS subscription revenue allocations for the Luxembourg SARL at non-arm's length values to shift profits to low-tax or zero-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD adjusts taxable income upward under Article 56bis LIR and OECD TP rules. A 10% penalty on the additional assessment may be imposed, plus monthly late interest. Corresponding adjustments may be denied where documentation is insufficient.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign returns without reviewing TP documentation, or who approve fabricated TP analyses, may be civilly liable for the additional tax and penalties. Intentional mispricing is tax fraud and can result in criminal fines, director imprisonment, and travel restrictions during investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Luxembourg SARL as a letterbox entity with no local office, staff, decision-making, or substantive operational control over the cybersecurity SaaS product, IP, or financing flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD may apply the GAAR to disregard the entity, re-attribute income to the beneficial owners, deny treaty benefits, and reclassify transactions. The minimum net wealth tax may be increased to EUR 3,210 where substance tests are not met; VAT deregistration and reputational sanctions may follow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil liability for trading debts where the entity is used heterogeneously or as a façade; criminal complicity in tax evasion may lead to personal fines, travel bans, and imprisonment. The corporate veil is pierced for deliberate abuse, allowing attachment of personal estates.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing SaaS subscription payments from higher-risk sources, providing penetration-testing services that facilitate unauthorized access, or failing to conduct adequate customer-due-diligence and transaction screening under Luxembourg AML law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the amended Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF supervisory practice, administrative fines up to EUR 5 million or 10% of annual turnover; criminal penalties for laundering include imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and fines up to EUR 1 million; asset freezing and public sanction registers apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners can be personally prosecuted for AML failures. Regulatory prohibition on holding management functions, travel bans pending proceedings, and restitution orders against personal assets are possible. The corporate veil is pierced for severe compliance failures.
